reviews.text: 天赋树挺大的. 这游戏很轻松. 挺好玩.

Nice game, fair price! A few more levels to max out the skill tree would have been nice or at least an option to go back and play the levels all over after finishing the final one, maybe even with increased enemy health for some more content or endless mode.
不太好玩
The only "idle" feature is taking forever to progress. Basically no content and seemingly no offline progression. Pretty lousy.

Could use some rebalancing; I liked being able to adjust the tower layouts to work towards the killstreak (without immediately failing a level if one minion gets to the castle). I was planning to keep playing when I saw the 'finish game in under 4 hours' achievement. WHY would you add a speedrunning achievement to a casual/idler game? Not going to bother playing it again if I can't get 100% out of it.

It's a good game up until 20ish, where you just run into a difficulty wall. The dev(s) say that they're looking at rebalancing, but that'll only help partway. The other issue is the lack of any information at all. We have no idea what hp any enemy has, what damage the towers do, or any base stats on anything. How are we supposed to have any idea what's worthwhile without having to prestige and spend an hour or more rebuilding to get back to where we were. It's very lazy. It's also a $3 game so I'm not angry about it, but it stops it from being 'good'.
pretty cool and unique tower defense game. There is no health bar for your tower. All you need to do is farm money upgrade towers. The strategy is how you spend diamonds to upgrade your prestige.

Edit to respond to developer: No. I played with these updates. I literally quit playing seconds before this review. I quit playing specifically to write the review. It was April 30th, after the updates. It's still wildly unbalanced. I started a new file today, May 2, just to prove to myself that I wasn't just being a stubborn a-hole or something and that the game itself was indeed broken. I gave it a very fair shot because I hate writing negative reviews. I went back to my original save and it's still going for hours to get to level 32. It's still broken and I'm not wasting anymore time on it. kameronmd nailed my thoughts on this. I was so hype for more fun levels after I played the demo. I don't often play this type of game but I really had fun with the demo. I liked the art style, the simplicity, the prestige tree, etc. Its genuinely fun to play up to level 20. Then you hit a hard wall that ruins any fun you were having at all. I have literally left my game on for days trying to rack up enough money to buy enough prestige stuff to get to the next level. A lot of them are useless and don't meaningfully help you. Its called castle idler but it isn't idle at all until you get to level 20; at that point you just wait and VERY SLOWLY upgrade your stats, having to replay the same levels for hours before getting to the one you actually left off on; it's awful. Don't waste your money or your TIME. I'm more livid about the time sink than anything, it's pointless and it's not fun. Just have a nice time playing the demo or quit when you get to level 20. Awful

Big fan of Idler games, especially ones with achievements! Whilst I'm working or whenever I'm playing something else, Idlers are the best. Found the demo a month or so again and it was exactly the game I was looking for, not too difficult but a little bit time consuming. Managed to get all achievements after 60~ hours, 100% worth the few bucks.
3小时通关，挺不错的塔防小品，玩着很舒服。需要注意的是本作实际上是偏解谜的本格塔防，有设计好的固定格子和数值递进，“放置”和“挂机”的标签完全错误，只借了放置游戏的声望转生机制。 30关之后的打法逻辑是：冰塔上毒、切割叠层、炸弹收割，再补充尖塔和火焰的伤害乘区，每个塔都起到了应有的作用。

Castle Idler, developed and published by Soy Boy Games, is a compact and thoughtfully designed hybrid that merges the satisfying loops of idle games with the familiar structure of tower defense. Rather than leaning into high-pressure strategy or complex mechanics, it adopts a more relaxed philosophy, inviting players to gradually build up their defenses, optimize resource flow, and watch their systems evolve over time. The result is a game that feels approachable from the very beginning, yet still offers enough progression hooks to keep players engaged across multiple runs. The core gameplay revolves around placing defensive towers along a fixed path while a continuous stream of enemies marches toward the castle. Unlike traditional tower defense games that rely on distinct waves with downtime in between, Castle Idler removes that structure entirely. Enemies arrive in a steady, uninterrupted flow, shifting the focus from reactive decision-making to long-term efficiency. This design choice changes the pacing in a meaningful way, creating a more laid-back experience where players are constantly tweaking and improving rather than scrambling to survive sudden spikes in difficulty. It aligns naturally with the idle genre, encouraging a sense of steady growth rather than moment-to-moment tension. Progression is where the game finds much of its strength. As players defeat enemies and gather resources, they unlock upgrades that enhance tower effectiveness, increase resource generation, and introduce new strategic options. The inclusion of a prestige system adds another layer of depth, allowing players to reset their progress in exchange for permanent bonuses that accelerate future runs. This loop of building up, resetting, and returning stronger is executed well, providing a tangible sense of advancement even when individual runs begin to plateau. Each prestige cycle feels meaningful, as previously challenging sections become easier and more efficient to manage. Despite this solid foundation, the balance is not entirely consistent throughout. The early and mid-game stages feel well-paced, with a steady stream of upgrades and improvements that keep the experience rewarding. However, as players push further, the progression curve can become uneven. Certain sections may feel like they require disproportionate grinding, slowing down the otherwise smooth rhythm of the game. This can momentarily disrupt the sense of flow that idle games rely on, making later stages feel more like a hurdle than a natural extension of the progression system. Visually, Castle Idler embraces a minimalist pixel art style that prioritizes clarity and charm over complexity. The environments are simple but colorful, and the units are easy to distinguish, ensuring that players can quickly understand what is happening on screen even as the action intensifies. The clean presentation works well for an idle-focused experience, as it avoids overwhelming the player while still maintaining a pleasant aesthetic. It may not be visually groundbreaking, but it is cohesive and functional in a way that suits the game’s design philosophy. The audio design follows a similarly restrained approach. Background music is calm and unobtrusive, complementing the game’s relaxed pace without drawing too much attention. Sound effects provide feedback for tower attacks and enemy interactions, though they remain fairly basic. While the audio does not stand out as a defining feature, it supports the overall atmosphere effectively, reinforcing the game’s identity as a low-pressure, incremental experience. One of the more notable aspects of Castle Idler is its relatively short length. Unlike many idle games that are designed for long-term play over days or weeks, this title can be experienced in a much shorter timeframe. This gives it a focused, almost self-contained feel, making it ideal for players who want the satisfaction of an incremental game without a major time commitment. However, this also means that replayability is somewhat limited once all upgrades have been unlocked and the core systems have been fully explored. Overall, Castle Idler succeeds as a streamlined and accessible take on idle tower defense, offering a satisfying progression loop and a relaxed gameplay structure that sets it apart from more traditional entries in the genre. Its strengths lie in its intuitive design, rewarding prestige system, and unique continuous-flow enemy system, while its weaknesses stem from occasional balance issues and limited long-term depth. It is best approached as a concise and enjoyable experience rather than a game meant to be played indefinitely. Rating: 7/10

Much more akin to a puzzle than a game. On rails so tight, the devs nearly expect you to divine their original intent for just about every decision available in the "game". 1/5 - Neat concept, poor execution.

Seem to be a bunch of people complaining about this being hard... yes it can be, but not impossible. Finished. Yes, it made me think and I had to re-do my skills to work out better synergies to make progress more than a handful of times, in the later stages, clearing 1 level to get 1 more skill unlocked then having to reset was tough, but its doable. This game is not a simple invest everything in the 1 tower you like and then blitz the whole thing, you need to read through the skills, work out which ones to use based on the map and what you have access to, its not a simple straight progression, use your brain and it can be done.
Basically one way to progress, not enough variety to strategies and levels. Cool idea though
A little frustrating to progress in the endgame and definitely shouldn't really be considered an "idle game" but not bad.
no

Aesthetic is great and the little details in every bit of the animation goes a long way. After around floor 20 (30 minutes into playing), the scaling for enemies ramps up very quickly. To combat this, you have these very very powerful perks you can unlock except these perks only apply to one very specific weapon and nothing else will scale very well meaning you have to use that one weapon or leave your game running afk for an hour to grind and scale up. "My arrow towers do 20 DPS, my frost does about 5 but slows them down a ton. Oh look this upgrade makes my spinning blades deal 3000 DPS and enemies went from 50 HP to 50k, looks like im pretty much only using spinning blades." Grinding also doesn't feel very good because beating up enemies nets you very little unless you actually kill them but once you are able to kill them, you are always forced to go the next level and can't go back once you hit the kill count. Finished the game after about 3.5 hours. 6/10. Not bad but not great either.

Was the first person and fastest person to 100% this game! If you want an idle incremental experience, this game is NOT it. A lot of strategy and thinking is involved, and there's a lot of changing things up constantly. It could be frustrating for you. I'd only recommend it if you're looking for something to that's satisfying to accomplish but may take some time to get there. Finished? Yes Steam Achievements? Difficult game in general. Steam Deck? Perfect. Rating? 8/10 (it's just really difficult) My curator page: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45865425-CozyAriGames/ Full videos on Youtube.
数值做得跟屎一样

I want to recommend this, but I cannot. The game is unnecessarily short. an endless mode at the end where you stay on the same level but the enemies get stronger every time you beat enough of them would've been pretty cool. Because the last level as it is, is very easy. You cannot get every upgrade, so you have to pick between some that probably don't do anything late game anyway. (Starting with money is nice n' all, but that money is going to be quickly useless, choose something else.) This isn't an idle game, it's an active game with a lot of waiting. Most of my time spent on this game was on the second last level. Where I must not have chosen the right upgrades or something, because it just wasn't going well. Then eventually I tweaked it... and again.... and again.... and again.... and then suddenly I did the level flawlessly. But at the end of this game... it just ends. You get there, it's over. It leaves you wanting more. But you'd think that would be a good thing in the game, it must be fun, right? Unfortunately it only really starts to get fun just as it's ending. Maybe they'll update it, add more to it. I might revise this review. At least it gave me another game where I've got all the achievements. So that's nice. But as it currently is, it just feels incomplete. Which is how I felt going through the game and not being able to get every upgrade. As it currently is, I'd give it like a 4/10. It's a good game... it just feels unfinished.
A short idler with an interesting mechanic. You're essentially trying to create a defense line that is capable of killing everything coming its way.
[h1][b]Way too SHORT!!![/b][/h1]
This is a very bare-bones game with not very interesting mechanics.

It starts nice but in the later game it feels like a bad balance between a Tower Defense and an Incremental. It is too slow and limiting to be a good TD game, as things like the prestige mechanic and the money-farming prevent a satisfying use of strategy. Some of the levels are also too difficult to be a relaxing Idle game. The progression is very inconsistent. Sometimes, progression is fast and sometimes I found myself waiting several minutes without being able to do anything, and due to the Incremental nature of the game, you never know whether it's because you need to switch strategies or whether it's intended to just farm more before progressing. And you cannot switch builds without prestiging, which partially resets your progress again.

Really fun game, though I didn't expect I'd need to idle as long as I did. I ended up leaving it running, while I was at work, on the 3rd to last map to boost up money enough to get through it. At best I was getting a kill streak of 12 but it was enough to get some cash together to buy the damage I needed to finish the game. I'd say buy it if you like tower defense. There could be more to the "idler" portion but for the price, can't beat it.

Good blend of idle, incremental and tower defense which doesn't come easy At first it looked like an idle game where you just idle and let towers get stronger to progress But it has an incremental aspect where you prestige to take strong passives to progress further on the next run Then there is a tower defense aspect where you choose tower type and placement for synergy Only nitpick is some minor QoL like duration/range upgrade carryover and stage 30+ kinda limited to poison burn builds (that the last upgrade is too OP it trivialized the last stage)

I am not gonna finish this. It was fun for a while but the balance is not good enough for me to really care. Mostly it is just me trying to figure out what combination the dev imagined is the most effective. And that's really only because this far it seems like only one combination can do it. That or I am just not good. Which I am not.
Played a lot of idlers and a tower defense idler seem fun, but this is just boring (which I know sounds crazy for a idler). The prestige loop is unsatisfying and the tower defense is very basic.

This game is more of an incremental game than an idler. There is also alot of strategy involved. The game prioritizes trying different builds and prestiging again. It is not a game that is mindless like other idlers. It really scratched my problem solving itch.
不好玩 非常无聊

[h1] 披着增量放置皮的传统塔防闯关 [/h1] 游戏商店的简介中有这样一句话：[i] 《城堡放置》是一款简短轻松的无波次增量塔防游戏。 [/i]但实际玩下来，这其实是个既不轻松、又不增量，更不放置的游戏。 游戏的玩法是‌固定路线的解谜式塔防，胜利条件是连杀一定数量的敌人。当数量达标后，就会[b] 自动 [/b]进入下一关，游戏内一共有33关，并且每关的地形和塔位都会进行变动[spoiler] 虽然都很有既视感，但确实不一样（换句话说就是没啥大区分度） [/spoiler]，同时怪物的生命值每关都近乎成倍增长。 而这就带来了第一个问题： [h3] 不必要的重复操作 [/h3] 因为每关都是一张新地图，所以当你进入下一关之后就要对塔重新部署，而这游戏的波次是自动出的，也就是说在你新到一张图、布局还没看清的情况下，怪已经开始冒尖了。 在游戏中共有五种不同的基础塔，根据后续的Build可以往不同方向发展，而塔防游戏的升级机制就注定了在非资源溢出的情况下，这必然会是以某个塔为核心的四保一。 游戏的设计也确实如此，在布局合理的情况下伤害能升至原先的数倍乃至数十倍，这就刚需塔对敌人进行集火，而游戏中塔的攻击范围不一，从小范围到全图一应俱全，再搭配上仅能选择前后的脑溢血索敌和0部署时间的设计，这就意味着整个游戏过程中都在和敌人“抢滩登陆”。只要有怪物突破防线，立刻就会出现各打各的的情况，从而演变成一只怪都杀不死，金币获取大幅下降的恶性循环，而在能连杀的情况下又会很快步入下一关，进而继续上面的循环。 于是整个游戏体验下来给人的感觉就是心累，话虽如此，但如果是以通关为导向的话，并不会产生太多负面影响，其原因就在于游戏系统的整体设计： [h3] 浮于表面的增量设计 [/h3] 在许多情况下，增量游戏的设计都是和放置要素高度绑定的[spoiler] 例外也有，但这里不进行阐述 [/spoiler]，上文已经论述了它放置要素的缺陷，那么这是否算是一个增量游戏？既是，也不是。 以刻板的眼光来看，一款增量游戏会有什么特性呢？个人以为，应该有以下七点： [olist] [*]可通过简单重复劳动获取的资源 [*]逐级解锁、可以升级的建筑 [*]通过转生获取的全局加成 [*]以游戏中各种代币解锁的天赋树 [*]重置后效率或是自动化的显著存在感 [*]可触的软/硬上限 [*]指数增长的大数字 [/olist] 事实上，本作或多或少都有沾边，但体现出来却不尽如人意 虽然在转生中加入了“每当敌人被击中时获得金币”的成长内容，但这种低保就算在最后一关、完全成长完后也只在 百~千/s 这个程度蠕动。虽然击杀的收益大概在十几万左右，但如果能稳定造成击杀，又会很快步入下一关，也是一根筋变两头堵的设计了。 虽然五种塔都能通过金币进行升级各种属性，但相对于固定的金币获取，升级的金币需求是稳定的倍数，大概以伤害3倍、攻速2倍、特效3倍的每级需求翻倍增量。同时升级的数值给的全是相同的固定值（或者说基础值的百分比），也完全没有传统的每逢整数、或是特殊等级就会有里程碑突破等相关要素。这也是为什么上文说以通关为导向不会产生太多负面影响，因为在这种设计下，单局游戏内的属性很快就能达到它的软上限，然后再无寸进，几乎不存在你现在打不过挂一会就打过了这回事。 所以你可能看出来了，本作的设计理念更偏向于《糯米团子历代记》和《Kiwi Clicker》这种，依靠天赋树构筑Build来造成质变通关的类型。但抛开其他素质的差异不谈，实际天赋树的构筑也相当简单粗暴，体验完总结下来就五个字“易伤和数值”，最后一层更是演都不演了，直接来了个A一下debuff层数加倍的设计。 所以实际体验下来，你几乎体验不到增量游戏那种“指数级成长”的快感，涨的飞快的只有所需金币。而游戏总体的流程时间也支撑不起增量的玩法。但游戏宣传的“简短”倒确实名副其实，我总计游玩约40小时（大部分时间挂在后台），而第一次通关后重开新档，从头打到尾一共仅用时1小时55分钟。 总的来说这款游戏基本是为了增量而增量，为了放置而放置[spoiler] 什么教条主义游戏 [/spoiler]，本质小品闯关塔防。但从塔防游戏的角度看，这个价格（指20%off）买一个33关的小品塔防，也还算可以接受。如果是被塔防玩法吸引，见仁见智吧。但如果是和我一样冲放置玩法来的，那么回答是：[b] 完全不行 [/b]。
The idea is kind of there, but it is simply not fun
Very crude but fun puzzle game which similar to Gnorp Apologue. You should know the game tag is wrong. Tower defense puzzle with some incremental taste. Not an idler.

This is a puzzle game designed as a tower defense game. The difficulty in combining different prestige skills and the satisfaction of the broken prestige skill in the end game made this game good albeit short.
It has good mechanics and fun upgrades but the gameplay is not super engaging and it needs more completion and replay mindfulness
very enjoyable, cute and appreciate that chill pace. thank you for your hard work! <3
beat it in a day. Relaxing.

I like the aesthetics and the overall idea, I personally think the skill tree is the strongest part of the game and like that you cant have all skills simultaneously (though I suspect that I am in the minority with that opinion). I would suggest, if the developer is open to suggestions for future games or updates, to continue to add more depth to the maps and enemies, the tower defense genre has loads of interesting ways to make each level and enemy feel more impactful and it'd be nice to see some of that. This game also has idler in the title but as far as I can tell you would get almost no benefit from letting this idle for more than a couple minutes, its more of a incremental, you cant lose, tower defense mock up of a game. For just a few bucks, as long as you know what your getting (short, not really finished, but still a bit of fun) I'd say its worth it. Maybe not worth it if you are looking for traditional tower defense or idler mechanics.

In the past year I've played dozens of incremental/idle games, some good, some bad, but castle idler is the first one yet that I refuse to finish. It's incredibly boring, you can't farm gold because once you finish an objective the level instantly ends, even if you have gold the upgrades are more often than not meaningless, progression is stopped by prestige which you'll have to do every 2 levels or the enemies will have so much HP you have no chance of killing anything. I'm sorry, but it's not fun and I cannot recommend this game at any price, play something else.
Very good synthesis of tower defence & idler mechanics. Absolute bargain.
It has good mechanics and fun upgrades but the gameplay is not super engaging and it needs more completion and replay mindfulness
